final_rationale: The verdict remains suspicious because the Actor did not provide genuinely new admissible evidence; they mainly reframed the same record and made concessions consistent with the initial audit concerns. That reframing is useful but does not cure the missing compliance predicate. Under the policy text, when the affected use case remains exposed, limited rollout, monitoring, and rollback are supportive controls but are not enough without either approved risk acceptance or completed disclosure of the material limitation before launch. The current record still shows an exposed below-target fraud dispute review segment, no approved risk acceptance covering that exposure, and no admissible proof that the required disclosure was completed. That means the case does not rise to compliant or compliant_with_caveats: the caveat here is not merely descriptive, it is an unresolved policy condition.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the required pre-launch disclosure for the fraud dispute review limitation was completed.
No approved risk acceptance addresses the fraud dispute review exposure; the only record is an unsigned draft that does not mention that exposure.
The affected fraud dispute review segment remains eligible in the initial 8% rollout, so rollout controls do not satisfy the policy predicate on their own.
The Actor's narrowed position still depends on a conditional future or assumed disclosure state rather than evidence that the condition was satisfied before launch.
